subject: compRelSEM(): how to name reliability coefficient in MTMM approach?

Hi everyone, I hope you are doing fine.

First of all, thanks to all contributors of lavaan and semTools for creating, updating and mantaining these wonderful tools. Also to the community for the conversations and lessons. It's great to be able to learn from you all.

Let's get to the issue at hand now. 

I've conducted a CFA using multitrait-multimethod (MTMM) approach. I've calculated the reliability coeficients using compRelSEM() from semTools. The issue now is that between all the different names for McDonald's Omega I'm confused and don't know how should I call it in the article that I'm writing. Does anyone know how it should be called? Hierarchical? Total?

I leave you down at the bottomg with the model, the cfa and the realibility prompts.

Thanks again!

modelo<-
'Aut=~eocd1b+eocd2a+eocd3b+eocd4b+eocd5b+eocd6a+eocd7a
Con=~eocd1a+eocd2b+eocd3c+eocd4a+eocd5c+eocd6b+eocd7c
Imp=~eocd1c+eocd2c+eocd3a+eocd4c+eocd5a+eocd6c+eocd7b
Aut~~Con
Aut~~Imp
Con~~Imp
#Residual correlation
eocd1c~~eocd1a
eocd1c~~eocd1b
eocd1a~~eocd1b
eocd2b~~eocd2a
eocd2b~~eocd2c
eocd2a~~eocd2c
eocd3c~~eocd3a
eocd3c~~eocd3b
eocd3a~~eocd3b
eocd4a~~eocd4b
eocd4a~~eocd4c
eocd4b~~eocd4c
eocd5a~~eocd5b
eocd5a~~eocd5c
eocd5b~~eocd5c
eocd6c~~eocd6a
eocd6c~~eocd6b
eocd6a~~eocd6b
eocd7b~~eocd7a
eocd7b~~eocd7c
eocd7a~~eocd7c'

fit.modelo <- cfa(modelo, data=base, std.lv=T, estimator = "ULS", ordered = T , orthogonal = F)

semTools::compRelSEM(tau.eq = F , fit.modelo , ord.scale = T)

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: compRelSEM(): how to name reliability coefficient in MTMM approach?
parts:
Because you only define your trait factors (letting your method variance be captured by residual covariances), you can only calculate "omega hierarchical" to define each trait's composite reliability.  That is the proportion of the composite's variance that is attributable to individual differences on the trait itself.  Each trait's (hierarchical) reliability should be returned in your compRelSEM() call.

Omega "total" is the proportion of a composite's variance that is due to both trait and method factors.  This aligns more closely with traditional definitions of reliability, which consider all reliable variance (even non-target variance).  If you are interested in obtaining omega total, you would have to fit a statistically equivalent model that defines 7 method factors for the 7 "eocd" indicator sets that you use.  Those factors should be orthogonal to (uncorrelated with) the trait factors, and in many cases you would also want method factors to be orthogonal to each other (at the very least, to prevent empirical underidentification).  Your correlated residuals imply uncorrelated method factors, so the model would be statistically equivalent (i.e., for each method, you estimate 3 factor loadings instead of 3 residual covariances). 
To obtain omega total for each trait's composite, you would need to call compRelSEM() once for each trait factor by adding the other 2 traits to the omit.factors= argument and setting return.total=TRUE.  Omega total would be labeled "total" in the output.

## omega total for Aut
compRelSEM(fit.modelo, tau.eq = FALSE , ord.scale = TRUE,
           omit.factors = c("Con","Imp"), return.total = TRUE)
## omega total for Con
compRelSEM(fit.modelo, tau.eq = FALSE , ord.scale = TRUE,
           omit.factors = c("Aut","Imp"), return.total = TRUE)
## omega total for Imp
compRelSEM(fit.modelo, tau.eq = FALSE , ord.scale = TRUE,
           omit.factors = c("Aut","Con"), return.total = TRUE)
